regionSwitchPlanMissing.^description: {$COUNT} account(s) have no Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) Region switch plan and no ARC routing control cluster. For a workload deployed across AWS Regions, ARC Region switch orchestrates the ordered failover steps (scaling, database promotion, DNS and traffic shifts) and routing control provides a highly available, data-plane-only switch for traffic. Without either, Region failover depends on ad-hoc manual runbooks that are slow and error-prone during a regional event. This is an informational DR-design signal: it is only relevant when the account hosts multi-Region workloads.
regionSwitchPlanMissing.shortDesc: Orchestrate multi-Region failover with ARC Region switch

regionSwitchPlanNeverExecuted.^description: {$COUNT} ARC Region switch plan(s) have never completed an execution. A Region switch plan that has never been run end to end may fail during a real regional event because of missing IAM permissions on the execution role, wrong resource references, untested manual-approval steps or a recovery time longer than the stated objective. Well-Architected REL13 recommends regularly testing the disaster recovery implementation; execute the plan (for example during a game day) and review the execution events.
regionSwitchPlanNeverExecuted.shortDesc: Test Region switch plans by executing them
